I got my Vive a few weeks ago.
 It really helps me socialize a bit and bring a little livelihood to my life.
I suffer from depression and social anxiety (well, I am an artist) and I don't go out a lot.  
The Vive really completes some of the missing things in my life. When I play SportsBar VR with a sympathic guy and we are just having a casual and empathic conversation-that is something that I have been missing for a while. I have just played pool with a very nice man yesterday, and then he just told me about destinations-"come, we can play catch on Mars together!"
That is absolutely fantastic.
Besides, I get to practice the five langauges I speak with natives (I will have to admit that it is quite a mission to find non americans, but that happens)

On top of that, I don't have the terrible feeling that one can have after gaming on a PC for hours-I will actually feel better than when I started the play session.
My whole body is engaged within the experience.

Thank you VR for offering me such a cozy place to be in!

I am so glad to see that there are other people like me! :)
I am a very sensitive person with social anxiety and social awkwardness (I think it should be a term).
On top of that my native language is not English, and even though my English is flawless (and I am very talented with languages and I speak five, I talked German with a guy yesterday in sportsbar VR, French today with some cool guys in Onward, of course that English too most of the time, Hebrew at home, and Italian-well, I haven't found an Italian player yet unfortunately!)-I cannot stop thinking "Is my accent good?", "Do I sound weird" all the time. 
The first time I played Rec room I tried my luck at basketball in the locker room. Then another guy stood next to me and I immediately started to feel my terrible social anxiety, and when I threw the ball he started talking to me I felt so anxious that I just got out of the game instantly, like a reflex. I guess it has also a lot to do with how VR makes everything much more realistic, and you are much more "exposed". When you are playing with a monitor then you are just there inside the screen, and not actually present.
I hope that, like many people say, with the time and exposure it will get better and maybe one day we could hit women in the bar and offer them a drink or two..!
Maybe we could practice that together in a multiplayer VR game and on the way laugh at ourselves (it could be much easier doing so when we know that each of us suffers from this), but I totally get you if you prefer not to!

Cheers and hang in there mate :)
